chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about a man who prays in a corner of the room, and his wife or his daughter prays beside him in the other corner. He said: It is not befitting for him to do that. But if there is a span's width between them, it suffices him.
He said: And I asked him about a man and a woman accompanying each other in a carriage, praying together. He said: No, but the man should pray first. So when he has prayed, the woman prays.

key_terms.يَتَزَامَلَانِ: accompanying each other / sharing the load

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for a husband and wife praying together in the same room or carriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the spatial and temporal arrangements for marital prayer, emphasizing modesty through physical separation; it specifies that while a minimal distance (a span) may suffice in a confined corner, simultaneous prayer is discouraged in favor of sequential prayer to avoid distraction. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining distinct spiritual focus (khushu') while preserving the social decorum of the household. The preference for the man praying first also aligns with the general principle of the husband's leadership in family rituals.
